title: Dedicated fleet autoscaler deviation & queue-protection postmortem and action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-12 a subset of dedicated customer pools experienced a sustained throughput shortfall and elevated queue lengths for ~3.5 hours. The incident surfaced as elevated latency and throttled requests for 7 customers (two flagged as high priority). Initial mitigation temporarily restored traffic by forcing a fallback to a warm spare model variant and enabling emergency horizontal scaling. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, interim mitigations, and a prioritized action list to prevent recurrence.
impact: Seven Dedicated tenants experienced degraded throughput and increased 95th/99th latency; two customers reported production errors and raised support tickets. Estimated lost request capacity ~18% across affected pools during the incident window. Revenue/SLAs impacted for two enterprise customers leading to an incident escalation to SEV2.
timeline:

2026-02-12 09:10 UTC - Request queues climb past threshold for pools A,B,C; first alerts to oncall

2026-02-12 09:40 UTC - Emergency fallback enabled: route affected tenants to warm spare variants and increase per-tenant concurrency limits
2026-02-12 10:02 UTC - Emergency horizontal scaling enabled via manual orchestration, additional nodes provisioned
2026-02-12 12:35 UTC - Traffic returns to normal; final remediation completed and monitoring stabilized

2026-02-20 15:00 UTC - Follow-up design review for long-term autoscaler changes
root_cause_analysis: Multiple contributing factors: 1) Autoscaler tuning relied primarily on aggregate host CPU and did not account for per-gpu token-serving saturation (KV cache/backpressure), so capacity decisions were blind to inference-level contention. 2) New kernel scheduling changes in runtime-2.2 increased burst token throughput variance for certain model families, causing temporary per-device saturation without corresponding CPU signal. 3) Queue-protection guardrails had conservative thresholds and an ordering bug that delayed fallback activation when several pools crossed thresholds concurrently. 4) Telemetry gap: the autoscaler did not ingest kernel-level saturation metrics due to a missing ingest pipeline configuration introduced during telemetry refactor (PR #8342).
mitigation_taken:
- Immediate: routed affected tenants to warm spare model variants and increased per-tenant concurrency limits to reduce queueing.
- Manual scaling: provisioned three additional nodes for affected dedicated pools.
- Monitoring: restored kernel-level telemetry ingestion and added temporary dashboards to track per-GPU token stalls.
- Post-incident: rolled back the kernel scheduling tweak for the most impacted model family in runtime-2.2 to reduce variance while we iterate on a fix.
long_term_plan: 1) Extend autoscaler signals to include per-device token-serving saturation, KV cache miss rates, and RK (request-kv) latency. 2) Implement multi-signal autoscaler that weights CPU, GPU token latency, and queue length with workload-aware thresholds. 3) Fix queue-protection ordering bug and add deterministic hysteresis to prevent thrash. 4) Add synthetic e2e canaries that exercise common long-tail sequences to detect variance introduced by kernel changes before rollout. 5) Release runtime-2.3 with guarded kernel scheduling changes behind feature flags and staged ramp.

postmortem_notes: Decision: Prioritize visibility+signals before aggressive autoscaler logic changes
Trade-off: Short-term rollback of kernel scheduling change increases tail latency modestly but reduces variance risk
Customer comms: Engineering dispatched targeted status notes to affected enterprise tenants; CS follow-ups scheduled
PR references: GitHub PRs - runtime#8342 (telemetry refactor), runtime#8420 (kernel scheduling tweak), orchestration#1894 (manual scaling helper)
validation_and_test_plan:
- Build autoscaler integration test harness that replays production request traces with injected kernel-saturation signals.
- Run multi-day soak with synthetic canaries and stress tests targeting KV cache pressure and burst token throughput.
- Run a staged rollout: feature flag + 1% then 10% ramp with automated rollback on canary regressions.
- Add regression alerting for sudden mismatch between CPU load and token-serving latency.
